"6.

The learned counsel for the respondents has drawn the attention of this Court to order dated 18.10.2022 wherein, it was recorded that the land involved in the present case was acquired by BCCL vide L.A. Case No.16 of 1984-85 and the persons eligible at the time of acquisition have been given employment, but at that time, the petitioner was only 5 years of age and therefore, there was no question of grant of any employment to the petitioner.
On that date, the petitioner sought adjournment to file a rejoinder to the counter- affidavit.
The rejoinder to the counter-affidavit has been filed, which is on record.

7. The specific case of the petitioner is that 2.46 acres of land belonged to the father of the petitioner since deceased was acquired by the State for the purposes of mining activities by BCCL in L.A. Case No.16 of 1984-85 and an award for compensation was also passed and the payment was also received by the father of the petitioner after executing the required bond dated 07.09.1999.

The father of the petitioner during his lifetime submitted representation for grant of service under Land Losers Scheme as back as on 27.07.1999, but no action was taken and thereafter, the petitioner filed several representations including representation dated 22.03.2007 (Annexure - 3),
but no action was taken.

8.It has been stated by the petitioner in para 7 that the petitioner sought certain information under Right to Information Act and in reply dated 06.11.2007, the case of the petitioner was forwarded to the concerned area and it was also stated that under L.A. Case No.16 of 1984-85 as many as 129 number of employment were provided.
It has also been stated in the writ petition that the father of the petitioner had furnished an undertaking that he would not challenge the award passed by the Land Acquisition Officer.

The petitioner has also stated in the writ petition at para 13 that the respondent authorities have informed the petitioner that 129 persons were already appointed for acquisition of land in the same mouza and consequently, the present writ petition has been filed.

9.The learned counsel for the respondents has opposed the aforesaid prayer by filing counter-affidavit and has submitted that the land was acquired and possession was taken as back as on 31.10.1987, but no claim was raised by the petitioner or his father purportedly on the ground that the petitioner was a minor and it was only after 22 years, the petitioner made a representation in the year 2007.
He submits that the petitioner was only 5 years of age in the year 1985 and was ineligible to apply for appointment.

He has also submitted that there is no vested right on the petitioner to have employment and about 37 years have already passed from the date of institution of L.A. Case No.16 of 1984-85.
10.

He has also relied upon a judgment passed by this Court in L.P.A No.353 of 2017 to submit that it has been held therein that if the land is acquired under Land Bikash Singh Choudhary Son Of Late ... vs Bharat Coking Coal Ltd.. 4. Today, when the case is taken up, the counsel for the petitioner is present.

During the course of argument it is not in dispute from the side of the petitioner that on the date of acquisition of land,
the petitioner was a minor.
Though, as per the respondents, the petitioner was 5 years of age but as per the petitioner he was 13 years of age on the date of acquisition of land.
Thus, it is clear that on the date of acquisition of land, the petitioner could not have been offered any employment.
No such provision has been placed by the petitioner that the respondents have any legal obligation to keep any vacancy reserved for those who were minor on the date of acquisition of land.

5. In L.P.A. No. 56 of 2018 (Shibu Rajwar versus Bharat Coking Coal Ltd.) also, it was an admitted fact that the claimant of employment was a minor at the time of acquisition and the petitioner in that case had claimed employment for his children in lieu of acquisition of land.

"8.

It is also admitted fact that at the time of acquisition of land, the children of the writ petitioner-appellant were minor, which fact is obvious from the conduct of the writ petitioner appellant that even though the land was acquired in the year 1989-90 but no such claim for employment has been made at that point of time but it is claimed by the writ petitioner appellant that several representation have been filed Bikash Singh Choudhary Son Of Late ... vs Bharat Coking Coal Ltd.. sentences.text: but save and except a representation said to have been submitted in the year 2012 no other representation has been annexed.

Even accepting that writ petitioner- appellant had submitted several representations but it is settled position of law that filing of representation will not be a sufficient cause in approaching the Court after such an inordinate delay. .........................................."
.............................Thus, the doctrine of delay and laches should not be lightly brushed aside.
A writ court is required to weigh the explanation offered and the acceptability of the same.
The Court should bear in mind that it is exercising an extraordinary and equitable jurisdiction.

As a constitutional Court it has a duty to protect the rights of the citizens but simultaneously it is to keep itself alive to the primary principle that when an aggrieved person, without adequate reason,
approaches the Court at his own leisure or pleasure, the Court would be under legal obligation to scrutinize whether the lis at a belated stage should be entertained or not.
Be it noted, delay comes in the way of equity.
In certain circumstances delay and laches may not be fatal but in most circumstances inordinate delay would only invite disaster for the litigant who knocks at the doors of the Court.

Delay reflects inactivity and inaction on the part of a litigant - a litigant who has forgotten the basic norms, namely, "procrastination is the greatest thief of time" and second, law does not permit one to sleep and rise like a phoenix.
Delay does bring in hazard and causes injury to the lis."

It was also observed in para 9 of the said judgement that in the date of acquisition of land the children of the writ petitioner were minor and were not eligible for employment and therefore the writ petition was filed after delay of 23 years.

The Hon'ble Division Bench ultimately dismissed the appeal filed by the writ petitioner and held that the writ court had rightly dismissed the writ petition on the ground of delay and latches being a court of equity.
This court finds that the present case is squarely covered against the writ petitioner by the aforesaid judgement passed in L.P.A. No. 56 of 2018.
6. From the facts of the present case, it is clear that the petitioner was a minor at the time of acquisition.
The acquisition was made as back as in the year 1984-85 and much time has elapsed and the writ petition has been filed in the year 2010 i.e after expiry of about 25 years.
As per the stand taken by the respondents, 129 persons were already appointed in lieu of acquisition of land.
